newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine denies deregulation plan report.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine denies deregulation plan report.

text.p: The government on Monday denied a report that it was considering applying a so-called "sunset provision" to regulations on business by which they would expire after five years unless the government renewed them.

"It would be inconceivable that there would be an automatic sunset provision on all regulations introduced into this House," deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said in answer to a parliamentary question from a Labour MP.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Roger Freeman, the minister in charge of deregulation, would suggest at Monday's cabinet meeting at Chequers that a pledge for a sunset provision should appear in the Conservative election manifesto. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
